model_annotation: The plot illustrates the accumulation correlation coefficient (ACC) as a function of co-occurrence number for several methods. The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and represents a linear scale ranging from 1.0 to 10000, with tick labels spaced by increments of 10. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” and represents a logarithmic scale, starting at 10 and increasing in increments of 10. A black solid line, representing the “Base” method, begins at approximately 35% and steadily increases to approximately 60% by the end of the x-axis. A light brown dashed line, representing the “MEND” method, begins at approximately 40% and increases to approximately 55% by the end of the x-axis. A cyan solid line, representing the “FT” method, begins at approximately 45% and increases to approximately 65% by the end of the x-axis. A green solid line, representing the “MEMIT” method, begins at approximately 40% and increases to approximately 60% by the end of the x-axis. A red solid line, representing the “IKE” method, begins at approximately 35% and increases to approximately 45% by the end of the x-axis. A forest green solid line, representing the “ROME” method, begins at approximately 40% and increases to approximately 50% by the end of the x-axis.
